$comment: A synthetic protocol, written the way the corpus's earlier generation writes one: actions live inside `classes.<name>.methods`, and the constructor is marked with `deploy`. It is the same document as `current/vaultlet.manifest.json`, which spells the container `contract_templates.<name>.actions` and the flag `is_constructor`. Both generations exist in the published corpus, and a wallet that read only one would be blind to the money the other locates. Kept small on purpose: it exercises the two declaration shapes, a deployment's fields, a covenant wired to a bare value, and a covenant hash that depends on another covenant hash — and nothing else.
description: A time-locked vault with a reserve covenant behind it.

vault.description: Where the vault's funds sit. Its address commits to the reserve covenant's script hash, so the reserve cannot be changed without moving the vault.

reserve.description: Where the vault pays out after its timeout. Its parameters are written in the deprecated `compile_params.` namespace, which one generation of the format uses where the next writes `instance.`.

guard.description: A covenant whose only parameter is the reserve's script hash. It is what makes this document's deployment fields a dependency rather than a list.

VAULT_AMOUNT.description: How much of it the vault was funded with.

TIMEOUT.description: Absolute block height the reserve becomes spendable at.

RESERVE_COV_HASH.description: sha256 of the reserve covenant's scriptPubKey. Computed by OpenVault.

GUARD_COV_HASH.description: sha256 of the guard covenant's scriptPubKey, which is itself built from RESERVE_COV_HASH. Computed by OpenVault.

OpenVault.description: Fund a new vault and record the deployment it creates.

Withdraw.description: Spend the vault back to the owner's wallet. Every value it compiles the vault with comes off the deployment; this action declares no parameters of its own.
